parsing.aliasResolution: A 9012 key may be the number or the alphabetic alias taken from the method name __p_<number>_<ALIAS>; both are stored in the tag map, so tag9012(1546) and tag9012(PQS) return the same value. Numbers >= 1500 are engine-internal. Keys with no parser (e.g. AUCTIONS, OCTC, TROWESWITCH, IGNORE_ARROWST_CHECK, USEDLP, BADSSR, NOPOST) are kept verbatim as 'unknown key' and are only visible to config rule conditions.
parsing.expressionValues: A value starting with '$' is evaluated as an expression (top-level tags unless listed in noeval_fixtags, default '58 109 116 9603 9604'; 9012 sub-tags unless in noeval_9012tags).
parsing.paramGenerator: A 9012 key starting with pgen_char (default '!') is a parameter generator: the generator's output (a ^-list) replaces the key/value in place.
steps: stripFixTags: split on ';', each token split on the first '=' into key/value; empty values are dropped; a repeated top-level tag overwrites the earlier one EXCEPT 9012, whose repeats are concatenated with '^' (Parameters.java:10619-10657).
9050/9052 are appended to the 9012 value already seen, WITHOUT a '^' separator; if 9050/9052 occurs before any 9012 in the string its value is discarded (Parameters.java:10636-10643).

client order id from client_oid_tag (default 9604) or alt_client_oid_tag, client id from clientid_tag (default 109), staff id from staffid_tag (default 116); all top-level tags are kept in _fixtagmap (Parameters.java:11235-11267, AlgoConfig.java:3391-3400).
9060 + 9065 + 9066 are concatenated (no separator) into the sub-parameter string (Parameters.java:11270-11276).
parse900Tags: 9009 (open/close flags), 9001 (algorithm, via algo_shorthand_map), 9002/9003 (start/end; an 'x-HH:MM:SS' value keeps only the part after '-'), 9008 basket (Parameters.java:10680-10727).
9012 from this message is appended after any earlier 9012 (_tag9012 + '^' + new) so later segments win (Parameters.java:11278).
processAlgorithm: working algorithm = 9012 sub-tag 1 (ALGO) if seen, else 9001; may be converted by OPE scheduler / algo relay map (Parameters.java:10924-10961).
parseGreekTags: 9004-9007 (alpha/beta/gamma/delta) are mapped to algorithm-specific fields (Parameters.java:10758-10922).
parse9012: sub-tags split on '^' (honouring <tq>..</tq> quotes), each applied in order by its __p_ parser; later occurrences overwrite earlier ones (Parameters.java:1390-1484).

computeRelayAlgorithm (non-final), then every rule of ai.fixmsg.properties is evaluated top to bottom; each matching rule's fixmsg is re-parsed into the order immediately (combine_fix_msg_config=false) so last writer wins and later rules see earlier writes (FixMsgConfig.java:101-199).
9060 handling: COMPOUND -> compound config; 58/61=CUSTOM -> custom-convert config; otherwise -> sub-order parameters (setSubParameters) (Parameters.java:11340-11349).
CUSTOM conversion (58/61 starting with 'C'), validity check (invalid algorithm -> error), final relay computation, parametersFinalProcess, adjust (Parameters.java:11351-11408).
Errors: _err_msg or a KO (9012.1525) value makes checkForError() return a reject reason; the order is rejected (Parameters.java:12737-12745, FlexOrderStream.java:13330-13333).
parsing.notes: Rule file syntax: '<fixmsg> :: cond1, cond2, ...' (ConfigFilter with '::' and ','); optional 'IR=<n>;' prefix restricts a rule by relay state (0: order not relayed, 1: relayed, 2: parent not relayed, 3: parent relayed; FixMsgConfig.java:116-131,211-216). '<js>..</js>' fragments in the fixmsg or conditions are JavaScript evaluated with _param/_stock bound. Rules are skipped entirely for TESTORDER/FORCEORDER/PATH (FixMsgConfig.java:103).

relationships.title: 9012 sub-tag 1 (ALGO) overrides 9001
relationships.explanation: __p_1_ALGO sets the working algorithm and _algo_algorithm; processAlgorithm then uses _algo_algorithm in preference to the client 9001. 9001 is still reported as clientAlgorithm/tag9001. Skipped when OEO no_algo_tag is set for the current algorithm.

relationships.title: Config rules rewriting 9001 have no effect when the order carries 9012 ALGO
relationships.explanation: Rules such as '9001=PEG;...' (HK SDMA short sell) re-run parse900Tags, but processAlgorithm keeps using _algo_algorithm from 9012.1 and returns early because the processed algo string is unchanged; only clientAlgorithm changes. The rest of the rule's 9012 still applies.

relationships.title: 9012.2 overrides 9002 start time
relationships.explanation: 9002 is parsed in parse900Tags before parse9012; __p_2 then sets the start again (or a relative start_open offset for values ending s/m/h).

relationships.title: 9012.3 overrides 9003 end time
relationships.explanation: Same order of parsing as start time: __p_3 resets _endstamp/_tag9003.

relationships.title: Explicit 9012 rates/aggression beat the 9004-9007 greeks
relationships.explanation: parseGreekTags runs before parse9012, so 9012.4 (aggression), .5 (min part), .6 (max part), .9 (max lit part) and .16 (max work rate) overwrite whatever the greeks mapped to the same fields.

relationships.title: Greek tags mean different things per algorithm
relationships.explanation: 9004-9007 are generic: e.g. 9005 is max part for VWAP/TMX/PART, min part for LINE, lit target for PART2 and a venue-bit mask for SHADOW/NINJA (0 -> -1); 9007 is i-would for VWAP/TMX/PART but max part for LINE/PCAP and min part for SHADOW. Changing 9001 (by client or config rule) re-interprets the same greek values.

relationships.title: 9050/9052 are glued onto 9012 without separator and lost if placed before 9012
relationships.explanation: stripFixTags appends the 9050/9052 value directly to the 9012 value seen so far (val0 + val, no '^'), so it must begin with '^' to start a new sub-tag; if 9012 has not been seen yet the value becomes null and is dropped.

relationships.title: Repeated 9012 segments are merged; later sub-tags win
relationships.explanation: Multiple 9012 tags are concatenated with '^' and parsed left to right; each __p_ parser overwrites the field, so the last occurrence of a sub-tag wins.

relationships.title: Config rules override client 9012 values unless null-guarded
relationships.explanation: Every matching rule in ai.fixmsg.properties is re-parsed into the order immediately and its 9012 appended after the client's (_tag9012 + '^' + rule9012), so a rule's value beats the client's for the same sub-tag. Rules guarded with tag9012(X)=null only fill gaps. Last matching rule wins.

relationships.title: combine_fix_msg_config=true changes every null-guard
relationships.explanation: With combine mode, rule conditions are evaluated against the original order and all writes are applied once at the end; null-guarded rules that are dead today (C-06..C-10) come alive.

relationships.title: 9060 role depends on the algorithm
relationships.explanation: If the working algorithm is COMPOUND, 9060(+9065+9066) is the compound config; else if 58 or 61 equals CUSTOM it is the CUSTOM conversion table; otherwise it becomes the parameters of the relayed sub-order (setSubParameters, which copies size/side/basket/ids and parses with the relay as parent). Strings shorter than 5 chars are ignored. Without 9060, 9012.60 is used with '~'->'=' and '|'->'^'.

relationships.title: COMPOUND needs 9060 and 139 (mode)
relationships.explanation: 139 picks the tracker: 1/6/7 position, 2/3 time (e.g. 'T,08:00:00_...'), 5 portfolio/pair (adds 1=PAIR to legs), other numeric < 100 price/algo tracker, or a named JS trigger (e.g. TrowePreopen) -> mode 100. Invalid 139 rejects ('invalid compound algo mode tag139').

relationships.title: Compound switch fraction requires client algo SWITCHER
relationships.explanation: With 105>0 the order is rejected unless clientAlgorithm is SWITCHER, a compound algo tracker exists, 105<=1 and there are exactly 2 thresholds (>=0).

relationships.title: CUSTOM conversion via 58/61 + 9060
relationships.explanation: If 58 (market cap) or 61 (%ADV) starts with 'C', after config rules adjustConvertADVAndCAP picks a leg from the 9060 thresholds (value = 100*size/ADV when 61 starts with C and ADV>0, else market cap in $bn) and re-parses the order with that leg's 9012; 61=C-TSW uses a built-in TSW table (PASS/LINE/SHADOWMIN by cap and %ADV, adds 23=1 if must-complete). Relay convertAlgo is bypassed for these orders.

relationships.title: CUSTOM conversion result REJECT rejects the order
relationships.explanation: A conversion result starting with REJECT (any case) sets _err_msg 'CUSTOM Convert to:<result>'. C-TSW returns 'reject: ...' when ADV < round lot, cap missing, or size outside the 0-5% ADV ranges.

relationships.title: AUCTIONS=0 forces 14=0, 15=0, 171=0
relationships.explanation: AUCTIONS has no engine parser (kept as an unknown key); a config rule turns it into 14=0^15=0^171=0 (no open, close or PM-open auction). Later rules can still overwrite 14/15.

relationships.title: AUCTIONS=1 forces 14=1, 15=1, 171=1
relationships.explanation: Config rule turns on open, close and PM-open auction participation.

relationships.title: 14=0 / 15=0 (or EO/EC=1) switch off the auction even if 9009 asks for it
relationships.explanation: moo_mode() returns 0 when 14==0, EO is set or 217>0; moc_mode() returns 0 when 15==0, EC is set or the order comes from DLP. 9009 and 14/15>0 can only switch participation on.

relationships.title: APAC orders without 9009/15 participate in the close by default
relationships.explanation: Config sets 15=1 when has9009=0 and inClose9015=-1 for the listed APAC markets.

relationships.title: 92 'O' with negative percent/ticks disables open auction
relationships.explanation: When the 92 limit-price string starts with 'O' and the percent and/or tick offsets are negative, 14 is forced to 0 (no MOO).

relationships.title: Moo rate type (217) > 0 before the open turns the order into a SMART_OPEN relay
relationships.explanation: setSmartOpenRelay makes the order relay SMART_OPEN; the open child is created as SMOO (also 276 for the PM open during lunch). moo_mode() returns 0 so the regular MOO path is not used. Skipped with no_relay_smoo or a parent relay.

relationships.title: 26/27 (moc rate/type) create a SMART_CLOSE relay when smart_close_compound is on
relationships.explanation: With smart_close_compound>=1, moc_rate_type>-1 and moc_rate>0 the order is relayed SMART_CLOSE (close child + intraday child).

relationships.title: 26 without 27 (or 27 without 26) is KO'd
relationships.explanation: Config KO 'tag 26 without tag 27' / 'tag 27 without tag 26' (except 27=4). Engine also rejects moc_rate>100 unless 27 is 8/18/38.

relationships.title: Indian close with 26=100,27=1 is reset to VWAP
relationships.explanation: setIndianCloseRelay: for IIS/MOC with an Indian close window, 100% MOC rate type 1 turns the order into a VWAP over the close-VWAP period with open/close participation off; otherwise it relays INDIAN_CLOSE.

relationships.title: 217/218 with 14=0 is KO'd
relationships.explanation: Config KO 'Tag 217 and 218 coexist with tag 14=0' (not under APIL/APIM).

relationships.title: 15=0 for an order starting after continuous end (JP/IN) is KO'd
relationships.explanation: Config KO '9012tag 15 0 after continuous end'.

relationships.title: VWAP/TMX arriving at the close become MOC
relationships.explanation: Config rewrites 9001=MOC for VWAP/TMX whose end is at/after close and that arrive within 2s of the close.

relationships.title: HK short-sell SDMA -> PEG with 152=1 (and 244=1)
relationships.explanation: The first rules in ai.fixmsg.properties set 244=1 (if unset) and rewrite 9001=PEG with 152=1 (no dark) so the SDMA-only rules below do not fire. The 244 rule must stay above the conversion because it tests algorithm=SDMA. See REL-G-ALGO-02 for the 9012.1 caveat.

relationships.explanation: Config KO 'cannot trade short sells in shadow for HK' unless the stock is an ETF/ETP.

relationships.explanation: Config sets 173=1^PPL=1 when RegSHO is enforced (2) and the stock is in a restricted state.

relationships.explanation: checkForError: 'aggression out of range'.

relationships.title: Participation bounds are validated
relationships.explanation: Rejected when max part > maxpart_reject (default 100), min part > minpart_reject (default 50), below the *_reject_min floors, min > max, max lit > max, or (PART) min part <= 0.

relationships.title: Dark-only (37) cannot have a min part rate <= 1%
relationships.explanation: checkForError 'min part level ... can not be combined with Dark Only'.

relationships.title: Cash balancing (13) is incompatible with i-would (10) and BernX-only (51=2)
relationships.explanation: checkForError: cash-balance cannot combine with iwould or BX-only; ratio tolerance and dollar bounds cannot coexist; aggressive NINJA with cash is rejected.

relationships.title: BernX-only (51=2) cannot combine with i-would, min part or open auction
relationships.explanation: checkForError 'BernX-only cannot combine with iwould or min part'; checkForErrorFinal 'BernX-only cannot combine with do open'. BX=2 also skips relay computation.

relationships.title: Buy-back (177) rules
relationships.explanation: Rejected on a sell, if EU and 177!=2, if NA and 177!=1, if open/close auction is on, or if 177=2 lacks an exchange ADV.

relationships.title: 92=R needs 70 (benchmark/price room)
relationships.explanation: checkForError 'no tag 70 with 92=R' / 'no tag 70 price room with 92=R'.

relationships.title: SCALE needs scale parameters
relationships.explanation: Rejected 'SCALE no input parameters' unless 100/101/109/102 is set.

relationships.title: PAIR needs a spread mode
relationships.explanation: Rejected 'pair no spread mode parameter'; spread mode 2 also needs a bps reference (63).

relationships.title: Unknown algorithm is rejected
relationships.explanation: After parsing, an invalid working algorithm sets 'invalid algorithm: ...'.

relationships.title: PART ignores 5/6: min and max are forced to the target rate
relationships.explanation: At the end of parse9012, PART sets max part = min part = target part (7 / 9005); PART2 does the same for the lit levels.

relationships.title: 7/8 before 1=PART2 in the same 9012 go to the non-lit fields
relationships.explanation: __p_7/__p_8 check whether the algorithm is already PART2 when they are parsed; sub-tags are applied left to right.

relationships.title: 9012.10 i-would price is ignored for WOW
relationships.explanation: __p_10 only stores the i-would price when the algorithm is not WOW; WOW takes its i-would bps from 9007.

relationships.title: Small orders can be moved to the OPE scheduler (off by default)
relationships.explanation: processAlgorithm converts small orders (size < ope_scheduler_size_cap, no cash, no relative child, no 287 offset) to OPE<algo> when listed in ope_scheduler_algos, or VWAP-family to TMX. Defaults are cap 0 and an empty list, so this is off unless configured.

relationships.title: Algo relay map may convert/relay the algorithm
relationships.explanation: processAlgorithm and computeRelayAlgorithm call Util.algoRelay().convertAlgo/relayAlgo(clientAlgo, 9012, basket); the result can replace the algorithm, append an opemsg and supply a compound config. The relay map class is not in the repo, so effects are not visible from the fixmsg alone. Relay is skipped for chain orders, cash orders and BX=2.

relationships.title: Large US SHADOW orders may be relayed SPLITMET
relationships.explanation: setSplitMET: US SHADOW with size > splitmet_sysorder_min_size, no cash, no min exec, no IOI, min part < 1 -> SPLITMET or random min-exec settings.

relationships.title: Config rules are re-applied to relay children
relationships.explanation: FlexOrderStream re-runs FixMsgConfig.parseFixMsg on child parameters (SMOO/MOC/split legs); rules prefixed IR=<n> or conditioned on parentRelayAlgo target only parents or children.

relationships.title: Sub-orders of a MOC parent are close-only
relationships.explanation: setSubParameters sets the child to doOpen=0, doClose=1 with EU after-close handling when the parent algorithm is MOC.

relationships.title: 188/189 turn IIS into a 2-leg compound (CIS)
relationships.explanation: convertCIS builds a compound config: IIS until the 188 time, then the 189 algo (default PCAP) with the same 9012 tags.

relationships.title: 197 (ladder) and 210 (stop loss) build a compound config
relationships.explanation: convertLadder/convertStopLoss write a 'C,4,...' compound config with algo mode 0; malformed values reject ('LADDER parameters invalid', 'Stop loss parameters invalid').

relationships.title: '$' values are evaluated, '!' keys are generators
relationships.explanation: Top-level values starting with '$' are evaluated (except noeval_fixtags 58 109 116 9603 9604); 9012 values likewise (except noeval_9012tags); keys starting with '!' call a parameter generator whose output replaces the pair (unknown generator rejects).

relationships.title: Client-algo templates are converted by config
relationships.explanation: Template client algorithms are rewritten to real algos per market/size: SENSATOLOWALPHA -> VWAP with 92/6 by %ADV, FMRPOP -> LINE/COMPOUND with market start times, KSPOP -> LINE/VWAP, STARSLTSC -> COMPOUND of PEG legs or PEG, DARK_KNIGHT (IN) -> LINE.

relationships.title: TROWESWITCH pre-open turns the order into a TrowePreopen compound
relationships.explanation: Under APIC before the open, TROWESWITCH=1/2 rewrites 9001=COMPOUND with a VWAP->LINE 9060 and 139=TrowePreopen (JS trigger ai.compoundtrigger_trowe_preopen.js, mode 100).

relationships.title: 9012 15=2 (or higher) passes every close gate but is dropped at the auction
relationships.explanation: __p_15 copies the value straight into _doclose, so 15=2 passes every entry gate that tests doClose()>0. ExecutionCustomizer then tests doClose()==1 for close-visibility candidates and drops anything else, logging (source_not_doclose). The order never reaches the closing auction and nothing warns you. Send 15=1 exactly.

relationships.title: 15=1 + 232 on a plain VWAP with no 27: the close goes to the scheduler and is never sized
relationships.explanation: Both mandatory close tags are set, but no doCloseOpe() trigger is (moc_rate_type defaults to -1, VWAP is not TMX, and so on). doCloseScheduler() therefore returns _doclose=1, so the opemoc flag in OrderHolder is false, opeMocSize is never computed and '<OPEprocessEOD>send MOC:' never appears. The order works out entirely in continuous trading. Fix: 9012=26=20^27=1^347=0 (or another doCloseOpe trigger). Seen on ETERNAL.IN.

relationships.title: Any 27>=0 hands close ownership to the OPE (doCloseOpe=1)
relationships.explanation: doCloseOpe() returns 1 as soon as moc_rate_type()>=0, unless 1513/OPEMOC is set explicitly. doCloseScheduler() then returns 0 (unless 368 sched_moc_mode>0), so the OPE/ConcertStrategy close path (opemoc, getMocSize, CloseWorker) owns the close instead of the scheduler. TMX orders are OPE-owned even without 27 (isTmx).

relationships.title: 1513/OPEMOC forces close ownership and overrides the seven automatic doCloseOpe() triggers
relationships.explanation: When _doclose_ope>=0, doCloseOpe() returns it verbatim. OPEMOC=0 moves the close to the scheduler/ExecutionCustomizer route. That route ignores stock.opened(), which is the weaker workaround for the never-opened defect, but it needs sched_moc_mode=0 and a scheduler :moc candidate. OPEMOC=1 forces the OPE. The config sets OPEMOC=1 for JP VWAP orders starting within 60 s of the close.

relationships.title: 368 sched_moc_mode>0 makes the scheduler own the close even when 27/TMX would hand it to the OPE
relationships.explanation: doCloseScheduler() returns 1 when sched_moc_mode() (first field of 368) is >0, before it checks doCloseOpe(). The OrderHolder opemoc flag (doCloseScheduler()==0) is then false, so OPE sizing from 26/27 is not used for the auction order.

relationships.title: 26=<pct>^27=1 reserves a fixed % of the order for the close and bypasses the maxpart cap
relationships.explanation: 27=1 makes the OPE own the close. 26 sets moc_rate, and OrderHolder sizes moc = size * moc_rate. getMocSize takes the moc_rate()>0 branch, which never sets checkmaxp, so the maxPartLevel cap does not apply. Types 1-5 are sized once and not revised (OrderHolder returns early once opeMocSize>=0). Pair with 347=0 on CAS markets. Outside IN, the config's 232=0 rule for VWAP with 27 in 0-3 also applies (see CLOSE-07).

relationships.title: VWAP with 27 in 0-3 outside India: the config forces 232=0
relationships.explanation: ai.fixmsg.properties writes 232=0 for algorithm=VWAP with moc_rate_type 0-3. Exempt: compositeExchangeCode=IN and 88=RVWAPRELATIVE/VWAP. A second rule does the same for VWAP with moc_rate_type>=20. The runbook's 26/27 recipe therefore zeroes a client-sent 232 on every market except IN. Rules are applied in order and the last writer wins. KS later restores 232=1 for non-short-sell close orders (L625).

relationships.title: End time (3) before continuousEnd silently resets 15=1 (and 232) to 0
relationships.explanation: During order validation, an endstamp before continuousEnd sets customtags_close=0. setDoClose(0) also zeroes _moc_mode. The only log is 'endstamp before close:'. If the client sent no end time (p_end blank in kdb), this gate cannot fire. EU also requires end>=continuousEnd and >preCloseBegin. Escapes: leave 3 unset or at/after continuousEnd, send 1866/PERD=1, or use 27 in the 20-29 band.

relationships.title: End time before the close + 15=1 is a hard reject on exchanges with reset_close_endstamp=0
relationships.explanation: The same end-time/close conflict that is a silent reset elsewhere becomes Gate 1: the order is rejected at entry with 'in close tag conflict with endstamp: <time>'.

relationships.title: 1866/PERD=1 keeps the close when the end time is before continuousEnd
relationships.explanation: prevent_endtime_reset_doclose>0 (on the order or its parent) skips the 'endstamp before close' reset, so 15=1 survives an early end time. The config sets PERD=1 for OCTC=1/2 orders unless EC=1.

relationships.title: 1505/EC=1 hard-disables the close: moc_mode() is always 0, whatever 15/232 say
relationships.explanation: _exclude_close makes moc_mode() return 0 on every call, so 15=1 and 232 are ignored. moc_mode() also returns 0 whenever 15=0 was sent.

relationships.title: 312 (send_residual_after_close) is not a close-auction tag; 312=3 also turns on reg-SHO handling for short sells
relationships.explanation: 312 targets the post-close/TAL session, not the closing auction, and is often confused with 15. On a short sell, 312=3 makes regSHO() true (enforceRegSHO>0, non-ETF), so 302 applies. With 302, 312=3 also skips the rawEndstamp rollback.

relationships.title: India: VWAP never enters the India close relay; that relay is IIS/MOC-only
relationships.explanation: setIndianCloseRelay() returns unless _algorithm.isIndianClose() (isIis()||isMoc()). On non-CAS names (closeVwapDuration()>0) the close is a synthetic VWAP window over the last N minutes, and closeMake is always null. That is expected, not a failure. An India close order should be clientAlgorithm=IIS (internal VWAP).

relationships.title: India CAS VWAP: config injects 347=1300, so the close reserve can arrive after continuous trading ends
relationships.explanation: 347/CSRC (close_shares_reserve_cutoff, seconds) delays the close reserve until preCloseEnd-347s. On CAS names preCloseEnd is the end of the auction, after continuous end, so 1300 s can land after continuous trading is over and nothing is held back. Send 347=0 (the guard needs >0), or a value larger than the gap between preCloseEnd and continuousEnd.

relationships.title: India CAS names: the config adds the CAS close settings (232=1, LCT=4, MILR/MCLR=2.9, SYNC=0, LCR=0, AUNS=2, TMX MOCB=200)
relationships.explanation: For CAS symbols (closeVwapDuration()<=0) the config writes 232=1 if 232 is null (with 15=1), applies the ±2.9% reference-price band (MILR/MCLR) and LCT=4 for priced orders, removes the synthetic close (SYNC=0), sets LCR=0/AUNS=2 for market orders, and MOCB=200 for TMX. These rules are inert for non-CAS names. This matches the SEBI CAS pricing logic (CAS reference price ±3% or the client limit, whichever is tighter).

relationships.title: India SILK (155=SG): MAXCD=0^MMAXS=0^SEB=0 makes the later IN MAXCD/MMAXS rules dead
relationships.explanation: L254 fires first and writes MAXCD(1627)=0, MMAXS(1517)=0 and SEB(1602)=0. The later rules (MAXCD=15000 for IN, MAXCD=60000 for TMX lag, MMAXS=1 for issue #74488) require the tag to be null, so they never apply to SILK flow. SEB=0 also sets the strict end-time buffer to zero tolerance.

relationships.title: TMX + 15=1 + 26: the order freezes for the rest of the day after its first fill gets it ahead of schedule
relationships.explanation: TMX is OPE-owned (doCloseScheduler()<1). With doClose>0 and tag26_deduct_scheduler_size() (moc_rate>0 AND the server flag, because T26DS is not sent), CandidateRegulator computes s = v1t/t12nc, a volume divided by milliseconds. This makes s about 1e7 times too small, so the schedule-deviation throttle never releases. Only the presence of 26>0 matters, not its value. Seen on SWIGGY.IN. VWAP takes the correct branch.

relationships.title: T26DS=0 avoids the TMX freeze while keeping the 26 close reservation
relationships.explanation: _tag26_deduct_scheduler_size>=0 overrides the server flag, so T26DS=0 makes tag26_deduct_scheduler_size() false and CandidateRegulator line 807 cannot be reached. EST_MOC is still sized. T26DS=1 forces the freeze path even when the server flag is off. The reverse TMX/VWAP rules inject T26DS=0. L576 injects T26DS=1 for C1/C2/CH PERD orders.

relationships.title: 27=10-19 with 26>0 converts the residual to a closing-auction order at continuous end, independently of 15
relationships.explanation: Every overtime/close authorisation is 'doClose()>0 || (moc_rate_type 10-19 && moc_rate>0)'. When the order reaches OVERTIME, overtimeHandling sends createAndScheduleEUMOCOrder(residualToMoc()) (LEFTOVER_TO_AUCTION). This happens even if 15=0 or 302 cancelled doClose. It is short-circuited only when moc_mode()>0.

relationships.title: Residual-to-MOC (27=10-19) ignores the max participation cap (6): the full residual goes into one auction print
relationships.explanation: The overtimeHandling guard that refuses to put an oversized balance into the auction applies only to moc_rate_type<10 or 30-39. With 27=10-19, MaxPart is never checked on the auction size, so an order held to 5% all day can send its whole balance to the close.

relationships.title: 27=10-19 is rejected where the closing auction does not start after continuous trading
relationships.explanation: Validation rejects with 'residual to moc conversion cannot be applied' if the market has a close and preCloseBegin is before continuousEnd. It is only legal where the call auction follows the continuous session (e.g. KRX).

relationships.title: 302 on a reg-SHO short sell cancels 15=1 and also wipes 232
relationships.explanation: setStockRegSHO() runs when regSHO() is true (sell short with enforceRegSHO>0 and regSHOState>0 or 312=3, or RSHO=1). If regsho_complete_buffer>0 and (302 second field>0, mustComplete, or a scheduled algo), it moves the endstamp to continuousEnd-302s and calls setDoClose(0). setDoClose(0) also zeroes _moc_mode (232). Any close then comes only from 27=10-19 residual conversion, without CloseWorker sizing.

relationships.title: RSHO=1 with 302: the 302 end time is a soft target and the order keeps working to the actual close
relationships.explanation: With always_reg_sho (or 312=3) the rawEndstamp rollback is skipped, so workorders stay alive to the real close. The endtime-expiry reject is also waived for always_reg_sho && 302>0. Result: aim to finish by close-302s, keep working, then convert the residual (if 27=10-19).

relationships.title: Korea RSHO=1 short-sell VWAP: config adds 302 and the residual-to-MOC template (26=100^27=10)
relationships.explanation: KS sell-short rules always add 327=2,0,10. With 15=1 and no 302 they add 302=900,1 (APIH also 302=600^SEB=0). With 302 present they add 112=0^MPO=5^STQD=5^26=100^27=10^SEB=0^MAXSD=0. So the template's 302 cancels 15=1, while 27=10 still sends the residual to the auction with no participation cap. To keep these orders out of the close, 26/27 must be removed; dropping 15 is not enough.

relationships.title: Malaysia short sells: config forces EC=1, so 15=1 has no effect
relationships.explanation: The config writes 9012=EC(1505)=1 for every MK sell short, and moc_mode() then returns 0. The MK RSHO VWAP rules also add 302=300,1 (or 302=600^SEB=0^STQD=5 on APIH) and SEB=0. With 154=1 they set 144=1, and on APIH 154=0.

relationships.title: HK short sell (non-ETF) without 15: VWAP/TMX get 15=1^173=2, every other algo gets 15=0^173=2
relationships.explanation: Unless the client sends 15, the algorithm decides close participation for HK short sells. Non-VWAP/TMX algos are excluded from the close (15=0), and every algo becomes passive-only mode 2. HK short sells also get PPL=1, LORT=0 and 164=0^LOR=0.

relationships.title: HK short-sell VWAP/TMX: config adds 23=0, 312=3 and 302, so its own 15=1 can be cancelled by the 302 reg-SHO reset
relationships.explanation: L280 writes STQD=5^SEB=0^23=0^312=3. L282/L284 write 302=900 (APIH) or 302=600. 312=3 makes regSHO() true for a non-ETF short sell when enforceRegSHO>0, so setStockRegSHO applies 302: the end moves to close-302s and doClose is reset (cancelling 15=1 from L135), while rawEndstamp is not rolled back. 23=0 is also one of the conditions of the 'prevent flip eod' guard (EOD-02). Not observed on a live order. Inferred from the rules and code.

relationships.title: 192 lead time needs EODBX (1686) at least as large, or the EOD flip only happens about 20 s before the close
relationships.explanation: 192=1,<ms> sets must_eod and the lead time (eod_venue_buffer_min). The EOD task is scheduled at continuousEnd-eod_venue_buffer_max (EODBX, server default about 20,000 ms). If EODBX is missing or smaller than the lead time, the task wakes too late and the requested lead time is never used. Set 192=1,X^EODBX=X (both in ms).

relationships.title: 23=0 + negative aggression + shares left/on close: the EOD flip is silently skipped
relationships.explanation: scheduleEODSetupTask returns without flipping (log 'prevent flip eod') when leaveAndOnClose()>0, aggression()<=-1 and explicitNotmustComplete() (raw 23=0). Remove 23=0 from templates that use 192/EODBX. This conflicts with the issueLastGoal recommendation to add 23=0 (FIN-02).

relationships.title: The EOD flip removes the PQS post-size cap and layer splitting, but stays passive
relationships.explanation: Before EOD, PQS (default 1) caps the posted size at about the size showing at the touch. After the flip the cap is removed, the full residual is posted as one order, and layers are bypassed. The order still does not cross the spread, and in APAC there is no EOD venue rerouting (that is North America only). Keep must_eod at 1. Values 2/3 unlock venue/pricing branches.

relationships.title: Passive-only (173) market LINE/PCAP/WOW/NINJA/PART without 23: FINISH leaves the order inert until the close
relationships.explanation: mustCompleteTag() defaults to -1 and the gate tests !=0, so with 23 omitted the must-complete finish branch runs for these algos on market orders. Once FINISH starts, issueLastGoal sends one 6-second take-everything goal. All later goals are dropped (IgnoreReason.ISSUED), and the queue/post goal is zeroed every cycle, so resting children are cancelled (goal_change). With 173 passive-only, no finishing take can run, so the order shows nothing until tryClose() at preCloseBegin. Seen on 285130.KP.

relationships.title: Explicit 23=0 keeps LINE/PCAP/WOW/NINJA/PART out of the must-complete FINISH branch
relationships.explanation: Only an explicit 23=0 sets mustCompleteTag()=0 and closes the gate. Trade-off: 23=0 is also a condition of the 'prevent flip eod' guard (EOD-02).

relationships.title: IIS never takes part in the opening auction; 14 (doOpen) is ignored
relationships.explanation: Validation forces customtags_open=0 for algotype().isIis() before setDoOpen. No parameter re-enables the open for IIS.

relationships.title: IIS joins the closing auction by default; 15=0 turns it off
relationships.explanation: Each region has an IIS branch that sets customtags_close=1 unless inClose9015()==0. IIS also keeps its close tags in the later filter that removes them from non-scheduled algos. Other things that also turn the IIS close off: an end time before the close, no closing auction, a start after preCloseEnd, or buy-back mode.

relationships.title: IIS with 209>0 becomes close-auction-only: no continuous trading
relationships.explanation: close_only_feature() is true for IIS with any 209>0. If the scheduler does not own the close, it stops producing continuous candidates. Any child that is not a close/qclose TIF is closed (CLOSE_INVALID), and the start estimate moves to preCloseBegin.

relationships.title: Stock never prints all session (locked limit-up/down): an OPE-owned close never runs
relationships.explanation: ConcertStrategy.recompute() returns from the !opened pre-open branch before tryClose(), which is the only way to setupMocWorker(). No CloseWorker is built and no close order is sent, so 15=1/232 are parsed but never read. The scheduler route (ExecutionCustomizer) ignores opened, so only orders with doCloseOpe()>0 are affected. Seen on 3659.JP.

relationships.title: 162=10 + 320=<sec> marks the stock as opened for this order N seconds after continuousBegin
relationships.explanation: 162>=10 sets ope_open_mode=value/10. If the stock has not printed, opeOpenStock() then copies it and calls setOpened() at continuousBegin+320s, so tryClose() can run (workaround for the never-opened defect). Side effect: with ope_open_mode>0, stockStatusChanged no longer preserves the order's opening strike or honours requires_individual_stock_object. Without 320 the OEO default buffer is used, and a value <=0 makes it a no-op. It does not lift the maxpart cap on the MOC.

relationships.title: 162=20 (ope_open_mode>1) forces opened 1 s into the session and gives up the opening auction
relationships.explanation: ope_open_buffer() is floored at 1000 ms when ope_open_mode>1, so a stock that has not opened is treated as opened at continuousBegin+1s. The first post-open pass stops the open worker (MOO_AFTER_OPEN), so MOO participation is lost on names that open late.

relationships.title: Compound 139=2 drops the first (auction) leg when the order arrives before the open
relationships.explanation: Mode 2 calls compoundTimeTracker().adjustTracker(stock.opened()), which removes the first phase for a pre-open order. The order then runs as pure VWAP with no auction leg. Use 139=3 (time tracker).

relationships.title: Compound time tracker (139=3): without the 'C' header the 9060 thresholds count from the order start, not the open
relationships.explanation: 9060 header 2 'C' measures thresholds from the start of continuous trading. Without it, an order sent at 08:30 with '1_' switches at 08:31, before the auction. Legs must be comma-separated (a '^' between header and legs does not parse). The numbers are start offsets, not leg numbers.

relationships.title: Compound leg 1=INLINE is rejected with SUBSYSORDER_ERROR (use LINE)
relationships.explanation: INLINE is not in the Algorithm enum or the shorthand map, so the leg resolves to UNKNOWN, fails validation, and the parent is rejected.

relationships.title: Open-auction leg without LOR: config injects 164=0^LOR=0, so the auction child is sent at price 0 and rejected
relationships.explanation: When LOR (1527) is null (outside NZ/PM/IJ/MK/C1/C2/CH/HK, and for HK short sells) the config writes 164=0^LOR=0. With both bands at 0, OpenWorker computes no auction limit, and the child is rejected with 'Invalid Order: Price is 0 but price mode is open'. Add 283=2^LOR=0.05 to the auction leg. Setting LOR also stops the rule from firing.

relationships.title: An SMOO leg needs 217>0, or no order is created
relationships.explanation: The sub-order relay goes to smart-open only if moo_rate_type() (217) is >0 and the stock has not opened. Otherwise an SMOO sub-param returns without creating an order. Re-creating the SMOO leg after the open creates nothing either.

relationships.title: 217 on a LINE leg (not the parent) keeps the leg LINE: it trades in continuous during the buffer and can finish the order before VWAP starts
relationships.explanation: relaySmartOpenOrder turns the leg into SMOO only when the parent carries 217. The LINE leg is created for the full remaining size and can send must_make takes after the open. On 669.HK it completed the order at open+4s, so no VWAP leg was ever created. Use an SMOO leg, or put 217^218 on the parent.

relationships.title: 139=<name> must match a registered compound trigger, or the order is rejected
relationships.explanation: A non-numeric 139 is looked up with RelayScheduler.getCompoundTrigger (case sensitive), for example PriceLevelSwitcher, Bracket9Switcher, SpreadTrigger or TrowePreopen. If no trigger has that name, _err_msg='invalid compound algo mode tag139:<value>'. A registered trigger sets compound mode 100.

relationships.title: 105 (compound switch fraction) needs client algo SWITCHER and a compound tracker
relationships.explanation: Validation returns 'compound switch need compound algo tracker' or 'compound switch need client algo SWITCHER', and also rejects >100%. SWITCHER (tags 74/105/106/108) is a live product that switches part of the order at a price. Do not reuse the name for trigger-based switchers.

relationships.title: COMPOUNDVWAP: an unfilled SELL at the end of warm-up locks into the aggressive leg for good
relationships.explanation: With price_mode 0 the decision price is avgPriceWithHistory(), which is 0.0 before any fill. Then pricemove=(1-0/ref)*sidesign=sidesign, so a sell gets -1 and goes to mode 2 (aggressive Inline). Mode 2 is terminal. An unfilled buy goes to passive mode 3 by luck. If refprice=0 the result is NaN and both sides take mode 3.

relationships.title: India dual listing: restricting venues with 155 does not switch child prices to that exchange's tick
relationships.explanation: Normal pricing uses the home exchange tick. The final rounding of a child sent to another listing's venue asks for that exchange's tick, but only gets it if server mixed_ticksize is 1-5 for the market (default 0 = home tick). Set 'mixed_ticksize: IN 1' to round IS children to the IS tick. Separately, feed_ticksize mode 2 (the current setting) lets the feed/MBREF tick table replace the local ai.ticksize.txt table, while modes 0/1 keep the local table.

relationships.title: GRANTHAM orders get 9012 144=1 when part-level capped
relationships.explanation: For client GRANTHAM with queue_mode>0, maxPartLevel (or maxLitPartLevel, in a second rule) between 0 and 50, and no 144 set, the rule adds 9012 144=1.

relationships.title: ELKCAP orders with 9012 55 get LCR=0.05 outside JP
relationships.explanation: For client ELKCAP, outside JP, when 9012 tag 55 is set and LCR is not, the rule adds LCR=0.05.

relationships.title: Non-ELKCAP orders with 9012 55 get LCR=0.05 (except IN / 155=SG)
relationships.explanation: For every client other than ELKCAP, when 9012 55 is set, LCR is unset, 155 is not SG and the market is not IN, the rule adds LCR=0.05. A separate JP rule adds LCR=0.05 for non-ELKCAP orders when 155!=SG, even if 55 is not set.

relationships.title: STEWFS orders get a default 9012 70
relationships.explanation: For client STEWFS with no 70, the rule sets 70=S,B,500. For an unpriced order that has not opened yet (price<0.00001, opened<1), the preceding rule sets 70=C,B,500. Both rules match such an order and the last writer wins (S,B,500).

relationships.title: 109 is copied into sub-parameter / converted orders
